turn2.differences: The author's three conditions (c1 ENG team, c2 private, c3 handles distributed systems) capture the team-identifying core of the request well. They omit two implicit but uncontested elements: (1) that a user named Priya Nair must exist to be added (only one such user, u-priya, exists, so no ambiguity there), and (2) that the action is team membership addition rather than some other association. Since the only candidates given are teams, the author's conditions are the operative ones for this exercise, and they match my step-1 reading. One caveat: the provided team records don't expose a visible 'private'/visibility field (truncated), so c2 can only be judged by inference from descriptive text (e.g., t-eng-public's 'wider org' wording) rather than a hard data field — this is a data-presentation limitation, not a flaw in the author's conditions.

ambiguity_effects.explain: Whether 'private' is a restrictive filter (implying a public ENG-named counterpart exists) or just descriptive doesn't change which team wins here: only one team (t-eng-public) carries clear textual signals of being the public/broad-audience one, so under either reading the same team (t-eng) still comes out ahead once c1 and c3 are also applied.

Reading 'ENG' as the team's key selects t-eng; reading it as a literal name match selects t-namesake. This is a genuine, unresolved ambiguity and it does change which single record is picked — the two candidates otherwise both plausibly 'handle distributed systems'.

Whether 'our' requires Jordan Lee's personal membership on the team versus just meaning 'the org's team' can't be adjudicated from the given data since no team-membership records are provided, so in practice this ambiguity doesn't change which candidate is selected from the available records.

turn2.naturalness_note: The phrasing reads like something a real Linear user would say — a colleague plausibly knows there's more than one team with 'engineering' in it and wants to clarify which one, using both an access-level cue (private) and a functional cue (distributed systems). Nothing about the wording signals it was constructed for a test.
